title: Compact-support exchange as a mate along finite horizontal arrows
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum and finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $p:X'\to X$, and $g:Y'\to Y$ be $k$-morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with $fp=gf'$, such that the square with vertical arrows $f',f$ and horizontal arrows $p,g$ is Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Assume $f$ is separated of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and $g$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then $p$ is finite. Use the ordinary pullback/direct-image adjunctions $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$ and $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$, with units $\eta_g,\eta_p$, of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. On the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], let $\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!\to Rf'_!Lp^*$ be the compactification-defined compact-support exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c$ of [def-exchange-projection], for a compactification $c$ of $f$ and its base change $c'$; by [fix-lem-exchanges], clause (4), it is independent of $c$ on these domains. Let
$$\chi:Rf_!Rp_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R(fp)_!=R(gf')_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf'_!$$
use the compact-support composition and proper-coincidence isomorphisms of [prop-functor-package]. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ the following equality holds:
$$Rg_*\bigl(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}\bigr)\circ\eta_{g,Rf_!K}
=\chi_{Lp^*K}\circ Rf_!(\eta_{p,K}):
Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rg_*Rf'_!Lp^*K.$$
Equivalently, the actual compact-support exchange is the inverse square mate, in the convention of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], of the composition isomorphism $\chi$.

source.place: Proof (β), finite-horizontal mate assertion; generalized from the Frobenius square to a Cartesian square with finite bottom arrow

proof.text: Write the chosen compactification as $X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{b}Y$, so that the original horizontal map is still denoted $p$. Write its base change as $X'\xrightarrow{j'}Z'\xrightarrow{b'}Y'$ and $q:Z'\to Z$. Both the open square $(j,j',q,p)$ and the proper square $(b,b',g,q)$ are Cartesian by the fibre-product construction. Apply finite-morphism permanence to $g$: both $p$ and $q$ are finite, hence proper. The original schemes and $Z,Z'$ are Noetherian: a field is Noetherian, the original schemes are finite type over it, and the proper ambient schemes are finite type over the original bases. They are quasi-separated, and all arrows used here, including the open inclusions, are qcqs by the cited permanence statement. Thus the proper/open and site-comparison lemmas below meet their scheme hypotheses.

source.place: Tags 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper); compactification diagram as in more-etale.tex Tag 0F7L (lemma-base-change-shriek)

proof.text:
First prove the identity on $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, writing $u^*$ for exact constant-module inverse image. The proper/open comparison for the Cartesian square $X'\xrightarrow{j'}Z'$, $X\xrightarrow{j}Z$, with proper verticals $p,q$, is
$$\gamma:j_!Rp_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*j'_!.$$
Use the specified map, not an arbitrary isomorphism: on a K-injective representative $J$ its defining map is $j_!p_*J\cong q_*j'_!J\to q_*I$, for $j'_!J\to I$ a K-injective resolution. This is precisely the normalized proper/open map in the cited theorem. On sheaves its first arrow is the identity identification of the two proper-support subsheaves of $(jp)_*=(qj')_*$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, first paragraph of proof and canonical proper-support identification

proof.text: Finite direct image is exact on abelian étale sheaves. It is also exact on constant-$A$ modules: forgetting the action commutes with direct image by evaluation, and kernels and sheafified cokernels have their underlying abelian kernels and cokernels. Therefore $Rp_*=p_*$ and $Rq_*=q_*$ on $D^+$, computed termwise, with their canonical units. The cited unit-compatible module/abelian derived comparison fixes this identification. The maps $j_!,j'_!$ and the constant-module inverse images are exact as well. Consequently the sheaf proper-support identification in Step 2 computes $\gamma$ on complexes degreewise: the last map $q_*j'_!J\to q_*I$ in its defining representative is the image under an exact functor of a quasi-isomorphism and becomes the canonical resolution identification.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, defining resolution map; finite direct-image exactness, and degreewise open-extension base change

proof.text:
Put $\beta:q^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!p^*$, the canonical open base-change map. On a module sheaf $F$ the following equation is an equality of sheaf maps:
$$Rq_*(\beta_F)\circ\eta_{q,j_!F}=\gamma_{p^*F}\circ j_!(\eta_{p,F}).\tag{O}$$
Indeed, evaluate on an étale $V\to Z$. By the proper-support description a section of $j_!F$ is a section $s$ of $F$ over $V\times_ZX$ with support proper over $V$. The left composite pulls $s$ to $(V\times_ZZ')\times_{Z'}X'=V\times_ZX'$ and regards it as a section extended by zero on $V\times_ZZ'$. The right composite first pulls the same $s$ along $V\times_ZX'\to V\times_ZX$, using the unit for $p$, and then uses the identity proper-support identification defining $\gamma$. Both give exactly this pulled-back section. The supports are admissible by the base-change and composition clauses of the support theorem; the pullback/open comparison is its canonical comparison. Equality is sectionwise and $A$-linear. Apply this identity to each term of a complex. Step 3 identifies all these termwise maps with the stated derived maps, giving (O) on $D^+$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, normalized proper/open map; support base change and composition; explicit sectionwise unit calculation

proof.text:
For the proper square set $E:g^*Rb_*\to Rb'_*q^*$ and let $\sigma:Rb_*Rq_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rb'_*$ be ordinary direct-image composition for $bq=gb'$. The ordinary exchange formula and mate-pasting give
$$E_M=\varepsilon_{g,Rb'_*q^*M}\circ g^*(\sigma_{q^*M})\circ g^*Rb_*(\eta_{q,M}).$$
Here is the normalization behind this use of pasting: the pullback square is $b'^*g^*\cong q^*b^*$; its vertical mate is exactly $E$ by the definition of unbounded exchange. Its conjugate under the two composite adjunctions is the direct-image square $Rb_*Rq_*\cong Rg_*Rb'_*$. Pasting along these adjunctions and then cancelling each adjacent unit--counit pair gives the displayed inverse-horizontal-mate formula. Equivalently one can transpose the displayed formula first under $b'^*\dashv Rb'_*$ and then under $g^*\dashv Rg_*$: naturality moves the units next to their counits, and both triangles leave $q^*(\varepsilon_{b,M})$ after $b'^*g^*Rb_*M\cong q^*b^*Rb_*M$, the defining transpose of $E$. These are the canonical composition comparisons, characterized by the composite adjunction, not newly chosen ones. Taking the $g$-adjoint of the displayed formula gives
$$Rg_*(E_M)\circ\eta_{g,Rb_*M}=\sigma_{q^*M}\circ Rb_*(\eta_{q,M}).\tag{P}$$
This last equality is the hom-bijection formula and the $g$ triangle identity.

On these compactifications $Rf_!=Rb_*j_!$, $Rf'_!=Rb'_*j'_!$, and $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=Rb'_*(\beta)\circ E j_!$. The canonical composition/proper-coincidence map in the statement, evaluated at $N\in D^+(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, is
$$\chi_N=\sigma_{j'_!N}\circ Rb_*(\gamma_N):Rb_*j_!Rp_*N\longrightarrow Rg_*Rb'_*j'_!N.\tag{C}$$
To see which compactifications compute it, for $fp$ use $(j',bq)$, for $f$ use $(j,b)$, and for the proper $p$ use $(1,p)$. The proper-input compact-support composition comparison is by definition the interchange $j_!Rp_*\xrightarrow{\gamma}Rq_*j'_!$ followed by $Rb_*Rq_*\cong R(bq)_*$. For $gf'$ use the same $(j',gb')=(j',bq)$, and the proper outer map $g$ gives only $R(gb')_*\cong Rg_*Rb'_*$. Thus their composite is exactly (C). This uses the proper-input composition theorem's explicit interchange normalization and the proper identification normalized by the identity-open compactification.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, displayed four-line model calculation; proper-input specialization and identity-open compactification

proof.text:
Apply (P) to $M=j_!K$, postcompose with $Rg_*Rb'_*(\beta_K)$, and use naturality of $\sigma$ at $\beta_K$. Equations (O) and (C) then give the full calculation, with composition read right to left:
$$\begin{aligned}
Rg_*(\operatorname{Ex}_!^c(K))\circ\eta_{g,Rb_*j_!K}
&=Rg_*Rb'_*(\beta_K)\circ\sigma_{q^*j_!K}\circ Rb_*(\eta_{q,j_!K})\\
&=\sigma_{j'_!p^*K}\circ Rb_*\bigl(Rq_*(\beta_K)\circ\eta_{q,j_!K}\bigr)\\
&=\sigma_{j'_!p^*K}\circ Rb_*(\gamma_{p^*K})\circ Rb_*j_!(\eta_{p,K})\\
&=\chi_{p^*K}\circ Rf_!(\eta_{p,K}).
\end{aligned}$$
This is the required identity at finite étale coefficients; no invertibility of an arbitrary exchange or faithfulness of arbitrary geometric pro-étale stalks is used in this calculation.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, compatibility omitted in the source; explicit substitution of the normalized equations (O), (P), and (C)

proof.text:
Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ be as in the statement. By constructible origin choose $L\in D^b_c(X_e,A)$ and $a:C_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, writing $C_T=\nu_T^*$. All arrows of the compactification diagram are qcqs by Step 1. Denote the canonical pullback and direct-image comparisons by $a_u:C_Uu_e^*\cong u_p^*C_V$ and $b_u:C_VRu_{e,*}\cong Ru_{p,*}C_U$. The canonical-mate theorem identifies $b_u$ as the mate of $a_u^{-1}$. Apply the square-mate unit identity with $L_1=u_e^*$, $L_2=u_p^*$, $G=C_V$, $H=C_U$, and $\alpha=a_u^{-1}$. It gives $b_{u,u_e^*M}C_V(\eta^e_{u,M})=Ru_{p,*}(a_{u,M}^{-1})\eta^p_{u,C_VM}$. Postcomposing with $Ru_{p,*}(a_{u,M})$ cancels the inverse pair, so
$$Ru_{p,*}(a_{u,M})\circ b_{u,u_e^*M}\circ C_V(\eta^e_{u,M})=\eta^p_{u,C_VM}.$$
This identifies the transported units for $u=p,g$ with the actual units.

source.place: Proof (β), finite-horizontal mate assertion; replacement of old Step 8 by explicit site-transport lemmas

proof.text: Use the open-base-change site-transport lemma for $(j,j',q,p)$: its equation identifies the specific $\beta^e$ in (O) with the specific $\beta^p$ in the pro-etale compactification formula. Use the finite proper/open site-transport lemma on the same square: its equation identifies $\gamma^e$ in (C) with the canonical open-adjunction map $\gamma^p$. The corners are Noetherian and $p,q$ finite by Step 1, so both lemmas apply. Ordinary direct-image comparisons commute with composition. For the proper square $(b,b',g,q)$ the transport-identifies-exchange theorem identifies the specified $E^e$ with the ambient pro-etale $E^p$. Together with naturality of $b_{b'}$ and $e_{j'}$, these equations carry $C_{Y'}$ of the etale composite $Rb'_*\beta^e\circ E^ej_!$ to the pro-etale composite $Rb'_*\beta^p\circ E^pj_!$, which is $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c$ of the statement by its definition; this transported compactification map is the pro-etale exchange named in the finite-level pro-etale exchange theorem, the map to which the exchange-coherence clause (4) of Step 10 applies. These are equalities of named morphisms, rather than choices of isomorphisms with the same endpoints.

source.place: Proof (β), finite-horizontal mate assertion; replacement of old Step 8 by explicit site-transport lemmas

proof.text: Apply the proper-factor composition site-transport lemma to the pairs $(p,f)$ and $(f',g)$ in composition order. The maps $p,g$ are proper by Step 1; the other maps are separated finite type. Use the compactifications of Step 6 and the comparison $c_f=C_YRf_!^e\cong Rf_!^pC_X$ specified by that lemma. Its composition equation and identity-open normalization say that the transported $\chi^e$ of (C) is exactly $\chi^p$ in the statement. The equation is valid for bounded-below $L$; no claim that the chosen etale origin has finite Tor amplitude is needed here. On the eventual $D^b_{ctf}$ domain, the operation package supplies the stated restrictions. Compactification independence on that domain is clause (4) of the exchange-coherence theorem.

source.place: Proof (β), finite-horizontal mate assertion; replacement of old Step 8 by explicit site-transport lemmas

proof.text:
Apply $C_Y$ to the equality in Step 7 for $L$ and identify its endpoints using the specified $b$, $a$, and $c$ comparisons from Steps 8–10. The units become the actual pro-etale units by Step 8, the exchange becomes $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c$ by Step 9, and $\chi^e$ becomes $\chi^p$ by Step 10. Functoriality of $C_Y$ preserves the composites; every intermediate comparison is adjacent to its inverse and cancels. Thus the result is exactly
$$Rg_*(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,C_XL})\circ\eta_{g,Rf_!C_XL}=\chi_{Lp^*C_XL}\circ Rf_!(\eta_{p,C_XL}).$$
Naturality of the two sides with respect to $a:C_XL\cong K$ conjugates this equality to the required equality for $K$.

source.place: Proof (β), finite-horizontal mate assertion; replacement of old Step 8 by explicit site-transport lemmas

proof.text:
Finally, put $G=Rf_!$, $H=Rf'_!$, $L_1=Lp^*$, $R_1=Rp_*$, $L_2=Lg^*$, $R_2=Rg_*$. The inverse square mate of $\chi:GR_1\to R_2H$ is
$$\widetilde E_K=\varepsilon_{g,H Lp^*K}\circ Lg^*\bigl(\chi_{Lp^*K}\circ Rf_!(\eta_{p,K})\bigr).$$
The proved equality says that $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}$ has exactly this $Lg^*\dashv Rg_*$ transpose. The adjunction bijection therefore gives $\operatorname{Ex}_!=\widetilde E$, which is the asserted equivalence with the inverse-square-mate formulation.
